script.base: Morning of 2025-10-05, outdoor, weather unsaved. Closing line BAL +2.5 / total 41.5 implies HOU 22.0 and BAL 19.5, so the book expects a low-scoring, competitive game with Houston a small favorite, not a blowout and not a 3.5-point dog-throw script. Lamar Jackson is Out, so Baltimore's base flow is Henry on early downs (31 carries / 115 yards over weeks 2-4, only 3.7 YPC) plus short/middle throws from an unnamed backup, not Lamar's 15 carries / 96 rush yards or Flowers' downfield shots (22 targets, 202 air yards). Houston still features Stroud to Nico Collins (26 targets, 235 yards, 298 air yards in weeks 2-4) while splitting runs between Chubb (34/128) and Marks (26/110). Pace is modest; garbage time is unlikely unless the Baltimore offense collapses.
script.flip1: Houston scores first and leads by two scores. Stroud and Collins attempts stall as Chubb and Marks drain the clock (the Dak-style stall case). Baltimore abandons the run, Henry's carry line dies, and the backup's only path is checkdowns to Hill (13 targets, -11 air yards L3) and Andrews.
script.flip2: Baltimore's 31% blitz gets home. Houston is -0.29 EPA/dropback vs blitz and +0.07 vs no blitz, and LT Trent Brown is Out, so pressure rises, deep yards fall, and the already-low total becomes a slog. Collins' vertical line dies; Schultz and Marks catches are the outlet. Henry still faces a Houston run defense at 4.38 YPC plus missing FB Patrick Ricard.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse pre-game injury report in the pack, not inactives (those lock ~90 min pre-kick; not in pack). BAL QB Lamar Jackson Out (Hamstring) removes 15 designed/scramble carries and 96 rush yards from weeks 2-4; pack does not name the backup, so his target tendencies are unknown. Designed runs tilt toward Derrick Henry, but FB Patrick Ricard Out (Calf), T Emery Jones Jr. Out (Shoulder) and T Ronnie Stanley Questionable (Ankle) mean worse blocking, more pressure, lower rush efficiency and more quick throws — gains for Andrews, Hill and Henry catches; losses for Flowers and Bateman downfield. BAL CB Marlon Humphrey Out (Calf) and CB Chidobe Awuzie Out (Hamstring) put both starting corners out, so Collins, Kirk and Hutchinson face uncharted backups; S Kyle Hamilton Questionable (Groin) would further help deep shots if he sits. LB Roquan Smith Out (Hamstring) is the TE/RB/slot tell: Schultz, Marks and Chubb in the hook and flat. LB Odafe Oweh Questionable (Eye) may trim the rush. WR Devontez Walker Questionable (Oblique) is a small target (5/39/49 L3). HOU DE Denico Autry Out and DT Foley Fatukasi Out soften the run front Henry faces; S Jaylen Reed Out helps Baltimore's middle/deep; T Trent Brown Out raises pressure on Stroud and hurts Chubb efficiency. No same-position snap-share history for the backups is in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location proxy only: BAL allows middle 8.5 YPA (34 att) vs left 6.56 (64) and right 6.25 (60). HOU allows middle 8.12 (32) vs left 5.16 (56) and right 5.48 (44). Both defenses bleed the middle, not the outside numbers.
matchup.pressure: BAL blitz rate 31%. HOU EPA/dropback is -0.29 vs blitz and +0.07 vs none, so pressure that gets home kills Collins' deep air (298 air yards on 26 targets, ~11.5 aDOT) and pushes catches to Schultz (106 air on 16 targets) and Marks (11 air on 8 targets). HOU blitzes 28%; the BAL EPA split (+0.10 vs blitz, +0.25 vs none) is Lamar's and does not transfer to the backup. Brown Out and Stanley/Jones issues raise pressure risk on both QBs.
matchup.bleeds: BAL run defense allows 4.91 YPC and 9 runs of 10+; pass explosives 14 plays / 162 yards on 20+ throws. HOU run defense is tighter at 4.38 YPC but has 11 runs of 10+ and 12 explosives / 143 yards, and is missing Autry and Fatukasi. Neither secondary is charted by position (WR1/slot/TE/RB).
matchup.overlap: Houston's primary is Collins, and the new overlap is personnel: both Baltimore starting CBs are out, and BAL has allowed 14 explosive passes. That is a vertical/personnel overlap, not a pure middle-of-field overlap. The cleaner zone overlap is Schultz (and Marks) into the 8.5 middle YPA with Roquan Smith out. On the other side, Andrews (17 targets, 112 air yards L3) overlaps Houston's 8.12 middle YPA and Reed being out; Flowers' 202 air yards do not, and the QB downgrade cuts against him.

Schultz last4 28, 29, 39, 30 and L3 16/98/106 (29+39+30) sits on the number, not a spike. BAL weeks 2-4: Henry 31/115 after a 169-yard week-1 outlier (last4 169, 23, 50, 42) — recent form is the 23/50/42 cluster, not 169. Flowers L3 22/162/202 (54 yds/g) vs a 74.5 line inflated by a 143; last4 143, 75, 13, 74. Andrews L3 17/123/112 is one 91-yard game plus 5, 2, 30 — do not treat 41 yds/g as stable. Hill rec last4 3, 18, 45, 41 with -11 air yards is a checkdown role, two big games, median exactly 29.5. No similar-defense or coverage-chart comps are in the pack.

edge_players.must_be_true: Collins and Stroud play full roles (neither is on the injury report), Humphrey and Awuzie stay out, and the game stays within the base script long enough that Houston does not spend the second half only handing to Chubb and Marks.

Hamilton playing and bracketing him is the other kill; he is only Questionable.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Baltimore blitzed early, Trent Brown's absence let the edge get home, and Stroud — already -0.29 EPA/dropback vs blitz — checked down instead of feeding Collins' 11.5 aDOT. Houston led by about a score and handed the ball to Chubb (34 carries already in the last three weeks) and Marks, so Collins finished in the 40s, under 65.5, which his 25- and 52-yard games already show is in range. Hamilton played and the unnamed backup corner was not a disaster. Schultz ran another 28-29 yard game: Roquan's replacement held the hook, Collins and the backs took the middle 8.5 YPA, and a 22-point Houston total never produced enough attempts for both a 66-yard WR1 and a 30-yard TE. The counter-case is real on price (none saved) and on pressure; it is not stronger than the two-CB injury read on Collins, so Collins stays flagged rather than cut, and Schultz stays a small lean only.
slip_story: One story: Houston has to throw in a close, low-total game against a back seven missing both starting corners and Roquan Smith. Collins over and Schultz over win together if Stroud has time; they lose together in flip 1 (clock-kill) or flip 2 (blitz slog) — do not add Chubb/Marks rush overs, a game under, or Baltimore downfield overs (Flowers, Bateman) to this slip. No second script. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player. Not a bet; no price, no stake.
